description: A test range on a red planet at sunset, and a data board. A launcher sends probes out over the range: find the median and the mean of their landings, pick the more consistent launcher, and read a box plot and a histogram. Then the drop tower: probabilities from equal bins, predictions from a run of drops, and two stages in a table of outcomes. Last, compare two launchers, estimate a batch from a random sample, and read a scatter plot's pattern, its outlier and its trend line. Plan an answer, run it, and see what it really gives. Every instruction is read aloud.
notes: Number Quest Unit 7 of the grades 6-8 street, The Test Range (grades 6 to 8): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.2.0 in the Space Base theme 1.0.0 at sunset (ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/launch-lab.test.js checks the literal map). The base (red ground, domes, towers, landing pads, landers, rovers, solar panels, wind turbines, craters and rocks) is the theme's own pieces and the pods on the results rack are its cargo pod; the rack, the launcher, the probe it sends out and the board's posts are the game's own simple meshes. The dot plots, box plots, bars, the drop tower and its probability line, the table of outcomes, the sample and the scatter plots are drawn by the game on one data board that always faces the player. Three chapters of six rounds (lesson mode: chapter=spread|chance|trend and lock=1): Spread Test (7.1: the median and the mean of the landings, the more consistent launcher, the interquartile range from a box plot, the mean absolute deviation, a count from a histogram), Drop Tower (7.2: a probability from equal bins, a prediction from a run's rate, a probability estimated from results, the chance of not, two stages in a table of outcomes, a model's prediction beside a real run) and Trend Watch (7.3: two medians apart, two means apart in mean absolute deviations, a random sample and its batch, the association of a scatter plot, its outlier, a prediction from a trend line). Plan first, then run: a stepper with a Run button, or three tiles; the board shows only the question until the plan is run; a wrong plan is run and drawn as it really turns out (a median line with more landings on one side, a total that does not match, a rate that is not the run's, a point off the trend line), with a spoken hint, and the round stays open. Every data set comes from a seeded generator and is checked by the game's test. Contexts are probes, launchers, bins and fins: nothing is priced, bought, sold, bet or won, and chance is never a wager. No timer, no lives, no fail state, nothing typed, no reward currency. Read-aloud is on by default (BRB.speak, friendly voice): lines are written the way they are said. Keys: arrows or + and - move the stepper (a held button repeats), Enter runs, 1 to 3 pick a tile. Each right round sets a pod on the results rack, and the sixth reports game over (won) once, which completes the course step. Saves only which chapters are finished. English only.
